content: New data from Tussell shows that UK public bodies spent £3.4 billion on private consultants in 2023–24—a 62% increase since 2019–20. Consultant spending remains significantly above pre-pandemic levels, posing a major challenge for the newly elected Labour government, which has pledged to cut such expenditure by half over the course of this parliament. Since Labour took office, approximately £650 million in new consultant contracts have been awarded, including a £223 million deal with KPMG to train civil servants for 15 months—the firm’s second-largest public sector contract. Labour peer and finance expert Prem Sikka criticized the trend, arguing that consultants often deliver minimal value and cannot meaningfully grasp complex organisational challenges in short timeframes.
